blocking_conflicts.title: A bare `git worktree prune` in game-dev-2d-shokunin destroys the 3 PINNED registrations
blocking_conflicts.detail: git worktree prune takes no path argument (`git worktree prune -h` -> usage: [-n] [-v] [--expire <expire>]) and is repo-wide. In game-dev-2d-shokunin it lists ALL FIVE registrations, including wt-r98/wt-r99/wt-r100, which the pin set says MUST survive. Executing the naive prune command against gd2d would remove the pins.
my_reproduction: -> Removing worktrees/r80-baseline-frozen-worktree | Removing worktrees/r81-frozen | Removing worktrees/game-dev-2d-shokunin-wt-r98 | Removing worktrees/game-dev-2d-shokunin-wt-r99 | Removing worktrees/game-dev-2d-shokunin-wt-r100
blocking_conflicts.required_mitigation: Either (a) `git worktree lock --reason '<r3 pin>' <each of the 3 pin paths>` before any bare prune (a locked registration is skipped), or (b) skip prune in gd2d and remove exactly the two UNPINNED registrations by path: `git worktree remove <path>` (works on an already-absent dir; S52/S61 both verified this on an isolated /tmp fixture). Mechanism (c) `--expire <ts>` is NOT-SAFE: S52 showed the split is incidental mtime luck and that `--expire '@2026-10-16'` silently pruned all five.
blocking_conflicts.corrected_sub_claim: S52 framed the risk as possible loss of the pin commits. S61 fixture-verified the opposite: prune deletes only .git/worktrees/<name>/ (index, ORIG_HEAD, worktree-local reflog, registration pointer); refs/heads/wt-r98|wt-r99|wt-r100 and their commits survive untouched. The residual harm of pruning a pin is loss of the materialisation pointer + worktree-local evidence, not data loss. Still blocking, lower blast radius than S52 stated.
